caseStudies.title: Case Study 1: Highway Infrastructure Overhaul
caseStudies.content:
A project manager is overseeing a multi-million-dollar project to overhaul a municipality’s highway infrastructure, including highways, bridges, and toll roads. The project is expected to take two years and involves multiple stakeholder groups, including engineers, inspectors, IT departments, construction crews, planning board members, government officials, insurance companies, suppliers, and union representatives.

At the start of the project, the project manager conducted a stakeholder analysis to develop a RACI (responsible, accountable, consulted, informed) matrix and a power/interest grid. Using this information, the project manager created a stakeholder engagement strategy and documented stakeholder expectations and communication preferences.

As project execution got underway, several challenges emerged. The highway laborers’ union raised safety concerns about the conditions on the worksite, while local government officials expressed frustration over increased traffic affecting residents’ daily commutes. At the same time, the IT department struggled to secure proprietary data while providing key stakeholders with the necessary access.

By the time the project reached closure, reports showed key performance indicators (KPIs) indicating low stakeholder satisfaction. The dissatisfaction resulted from a three-week schedule setback caused by equipment breakdowns, followed by shipment delays of the replacement parts. This ultimately resulted in a budget overrun.

caseStudies.title: Case Study 2: Software Company Acquisition
caseStudies.content:
A global software company is acquiring a publicly traded software development company with offices nationwide. The acquisition will enable the parent company to deliver greater value to its enterprise customers. Key stakeholders include the project sponsor, executives from both companies, IT and HR managers, and customers.

The project manager has been tasked with developing an integration strategy, which includes assembling an integration team, aligning product roadmaps, and managing the integration of HR systems. The project sponsor estimates that the project will take nine months to complete.

The two companies have distinct corporate cultures and operating models, making integration a considerable challenge. In addition, the project manager must ensure a seamless transition for customers. The project manager will collaborate with the IT manager to ensure that the various disparate network infrastructures and subsystems are compatible and successfully merged with minimal downtime for customers. Shared applications must be consolidated to reduce cost and enable the parent company to assume ownership. Team members from both companies must learn to operate the shared and consolidated applications.

questions.stem: What action should the project manager have taken to address stakeholder concerns and mitigate impacts on the project’s timeline and budget?  (Refer to the case study)

options.text: Enhance risk management by scheduling regular team meetings and ensuring clear communication with stakeholders.
Review the work breakdown structure (WBS) to determine the impact of the changes and update the document accordingly.
Incorporate resilience into the project management approach to help anticipate, respond to, and recover from risks.
Develop a collaborative problem-solving process to eliminate risk, ambiguity, and uncertainty from the project.

questions.solutionLine: C. Incorporate resilience into the project management approach to help anticipate, respond to, and recover from risks.
questions.explanation:
Projects rarely proceed exactly as planned; unforeseen factors such as changing requirements, stakeholder influences, or environmental disruptions can impact them. Resilience in a project context involves adaptability and the capacity to respond efficiently to unplanned events and adverse conditions. Incorporating resilience equips projects to absorb schedule or budget deviations and recover quickly, addressing stakeholder concerns effectively while minimizing negative impacts on timelines and costs.

The other options are incorrect.

Scheduling regular team meetings and providing adequate communication are helpful practices, but they are not enough on their own to improve risk management and prevent or recover from budget and timeline overruns.

Reviewing and revising the WBS would not sufficiently prevent or address risks that impact budgets and timelines.

It is not possible to eliminate risk, ambiguity, and uncertainty from a project of this scale.

questions.stem: What should the project manager have done when the highway laborers’ union raised safety concerns during construction? (Refer to the case study)

options.text: Use predictive analytics to anticipate risks and suggest effective mitigation strategies based on historical data.
Include training for the project's construction crews as part of the deliverables to enhance on-the-job safety.
Email the union representatives to request more information and clarification about their concerns.
Conduct information sessions to document the concerns and develop risk mitigation strategies.

questions.solutionLine: D. Conduct information sessions to document the concerns and develop risk mitigation strategies.
questions.explanation:
By documenting concerns, the project manager ensures that all issues are formally recognized and can be tracked. Formulating mitigation strategies based on those documented concerns demonstrates a structured, proactive approach to risk management, which is a key responsibility of the project manager.

The other options are too narrow and passive to serve as effective proactive risk management actions.

While using predictive analytics to anticipate risks is a valid technique, it focuses solely on data analysis rather than on direct, proactive engagement with stakeholders or the project environment to identify and address risks.

Including training in the project deliverables does not address the need to proactively identify and document the specific safety concerns or develop targeted mitigation strategies.

Simply requesting clarification via email may delay action, miss critical context, and does not provide the project manager with an opportunity to proactively engage stakeholders and develop actionable safety measures.

questions.stem: What actions should the project manager have taken to address the IT department’s security concerns and maintain the project's schedule? (Refer to the case study)

options.text: Request that the IT manager provide a detailed report stating their concerns and log them in the risk register.
Proceed with project execution, document the situation in the risk register, and notify the stakeholders.
Assess the impact of a safety breach, reprioritize tasks accordingly, and present options to stakeholders.
Implement an escalated risk response strategy because the issue falls outside the project's original scope.

questions.solutionLine: C. Assess the impact of a safety breach, reprioritize tasks accordingly, and present options to the stakeholders.
questions.explanation:
When a safety breach occurs, the project's objectives, resources, and stakeholders may be immediately affected. A thorough assessment of the impact ensures that it is understood and appropriately prioritized. This allows for the identification of vulnerable areas and the design of effective solutions. Reprioritizing tasks is critical because a breach often calls for immediate corrective action that may not align with previously planned priorities. Presenting options to stakeholders ensures transparency and inclusive decision-making. This approach proactively manages risks while maintaining the project schedule and keeping stakeholders informed.

The other options are less effective.

While asking the IT department manager for details and updating the risk register captures information, this approach is too passive and does not involve actively analyzing the impact or taking action to address the concerns.

Proceeding with execution without actively addressing the IT department’s data safety concerns could increase project risk and potentially cause delays or safety issues.

Escalating the risk without first assessing its impact, reprioritizing tasks, or presenting options to stakeholders is premature. Even if the issue seems outside the project scope, the project manager still has a responsibility to analyze its potential effect on the project and propose actionable responses.

questions.stem: What should the project manager have done to align stakeholder expectations with the project vision? (Refer to the case study)

options.text: Use audits and checklists to translate the project management plan into executable activities for quality assurance.
Adjust the project scope baseline to provide stakeholders with a clearer view of the actual results.
Establish a performance measurement baseline that includes flexibility in both the schedule and the cost baselines.
Define clear boundaries within the contractual agreements of third-party suppliers and contractors.

questions.solutionLine: A. Use audits and checklists to translate the project management plan into executable activities for quality assurance.
questions.explanation:
Audits and checklists bridge gaps between planning and execution, ensuring that activities and deliverables meet the intended standards and enhancing stakeholder trust and satisfaction. Implementing such measures demonstrates commitment to quality through consistent actions that align with project goals and broader organizational standards. By performing audits, project teams can confirm that processes comply with established policies, procedures, and standards outlined in the quality management plan. Checklists ensure that specific criteria and actions are consistently applied across various implementation activities. This helps stakeholders see their requirements and the broader project vision realized appropriately.

The other options are incorrect.

Adjusting the project scope baseline addresses changes after the fact rather than proactively managing stakeholder expectations.

Establishing a flexible performance measurement baseline addresses planning and tracking, not directly aligning stakeholder expectations or managing risk.

Setting contractual boundaries focuses on supplier and contractor obligations, not on aligning stakeholder expectations or project vision.

questions.stem: What should the project manager do to create opportunities for knowledge transfer among the software engineers? (Refer to the case study)

options.text: Encourage team members to ask questions of the engineers who have been with their companies the longest.
Foster open communication among the teams and promote team-building activities and mentoring relationships.
Conduct virtual surveys to encourage team members to share their expertise and experiences anonymously.
Schedule formal face-to-face meetings with both teams to provide a dedicated space for information sharing.

questions.solutionLine: B. Foster open communication among the teams and promote team-building activities and mentoring relationships.
questions.explanation:
Open communication ensures that critical information and expertise are shared effectively between teams. Software and IT professionals often have specialized technical knowledge that may not be accessible to other team members without deliberate effort. Mentoring relationships provide structured opportunities for transferring skills, tools, and methodologies, helping reduce silos in knowledge.

The other answers are less effective.

Focusing only on engineers who have been with their own companies the longest could unintentionally exclude valuable knowledge from other teams or newer engineers with relevant expertise.

Conducting virtual surveys is not an effective way to ensure knowledge transfer. This option does not build the trusting environment necessary for personal communication and knowledge sharing.

Scheduling formal face-to-face meetings can be intimidating and does not ensure personal communication. Face-to-face meetings may not be possible for all teams.

questions.stem: What can the project manager do to assess each organization's culture and help team members embrace the inevitable changes resulting from the merger? (Refer to the case study)

options.text: Offer team-building exercises, such as role-play, to demonstrate the other company's organizational culture.
Develop a program to implement change gradually, assisting team members in slowly adapting to the other organization’s culture.
Encourage team members to use dedicated communication platforms for real-time collaboration and information sharing.
Consider the unique characteristics of each team’s culture and tailor communication to maximize engagement.

questions.solutionLine: D. Consider the unique characteristics of each team’s culture and tailor communication to maximize engagement.
questions.explanation:
Considering each team’s unique cultural characteristics is essential. Organizational and team cultures influence how people communicate, interpret messages, and interact within a team environment. By adapting communication styles to align with the team's needs and preferences, a project manager can build stronger connections, minimize misunderstandings, and foster active participation.

The other options are incorrect.

Offering team-building and role-playing exercises could be awkward for some team members and considered offensive by others.

Implementing incremental change does not guarantee that team members understand, accept, or effectively integrate the new culture.

Encouraging team members to use dedicated communication platforms for real-time collaboration and information sharing would not lower resistance to change.

questions.stem: What should the project manager do to ensure that the expected project outcomes remain in alignment with the company's values? (Refer to the case study)

options.text: Monitor the project's strategic plan and update the goals and objectives to be achieved as the merger progresses.
Include a document at the start of the project that establishes a link between the project and the company's business objectives.
Review all aspects of project activities and how their execution is outlined in each company's integration project plans.
Ensure that all stakeholder concerns are understood and that they are guided through the changes resulting from the merger.

questions.solutionLine: D. Ensure that all stakeholder concerns are understood and that they are guided through the changes resulting from the merger.
questions.explanation:
Guiding stakeholders through a project's changes helps maintain focus on the value of the end result. Merger-related changes often redefine strategic priorities, operational processes, and organizational structures. Stakeholders might perceive these changes differently, with varying levels of understanding, support, or opposition. Addressing their concerns helps ensure alignment and shared commitment to the organization's new direction.

The other options are incorrect.

It is a good idea to monitor the project's strategic plan, but updating the goals and objectives to be achieved as the merger progresses means losing sight of the original intention of the merger.

A document that establishes a link between the project and the company's business objectives is part of the process of officially authorizing the start of the project. It does not ensure that the expected project outcomes remain aligned with the company's values.

Reviewing each company's integration project plans does not ensure that the expected project outcomes remain aligned with the company's values.

questions.stem:
A foreign government has expressed interest in owning a share of the newly merged company.

What should the project manager do in response to this development? (Refer to the case study)

options.text: Assess the impact on the project scope that may result from external investment.
Collaborate with the IT manager to implement necessary measures for network and data security.
Meet with key stakeholders to determine internal and external investment policies.
Revise the project’s business case to ensure alignment with changes in the organization's objectives.

questions.solutionLine: A. Assess the impact on the project scope that may result from external investment.
questions.explanation:
A foreign investment might come with specific goals, compliance requirements, or strategic priorities that differ from the original project assumptions, leading to significant changes in objectives, deliverables, or timelines. By analyzing the impact of foreign investment, the project manager can identify potential changes, risks, or adjustments needed to align the project with organizational objectives.

The other options are incorrect.

Data and network security should have been established and implemented during and after the merger. They should not be new issues caused by foreign investment.

Meeting with stakeholders about internal and external investment policies assumes that the organization has such policies and is not a step the project manager should take.

Decisions about investments should not impact the project’s business case.

questions.stem:
The project manager has been using story points to monitor progress. A burndown chart was created to present to stakeholders, highlighting the project’s performance over the past year.

What month did the team complete fewer story points than expected? (Refer to the chart)

options.text: January
March
November
December

questions.solutionLine: D. December
questions.explanation:
A burndown chart is a visual that shows how much work remains over time. Teams often use it in agile projects, especially during a sprint, to see whether they are on track to finish the work they have committed to.

The horizontal axis shows time, such as the days in a sprint. The vertical axis shows remaining work, which might be measured in story points, tasks, or hours. The chart begins with the total planned work. As the team completes work, the remaining amount should go down, creating a downward trend. A burndown chart usually includes an ideal line and an actual line. The ideal line represents a steady pace of completion from start to finish. The actual line shows what is really happening. If the actual line stays above the ideal line, the team may be behind schedule. If it drops below, the team may be ahead.

In December, the actual line is above the expected line, meaning there are more remaining story points than planned. This indicates the team completed fewer story points than planned and is behind schedule.

The other options are incorrect.

In January, the actual and expected lines are nearly identical, indicating the team is on track, with no meaningful variance.

In March, the actual line is below the expected line, meaning the team has fewer remaining story points than planned. This indicates they are ahead of schedule, not behind.

In November, the actual and expected lines are very close, but December shows a more significant variance.

media.alt: Burndown chart: expected vs actual remaining story points, January–December

questions.stem:
A commercial office building project has a total budget of $8,000,000 and a timeline of 24 months. At the 1-year mark, the project manager conducts a performance review and finds that more money than expected has been spent. (All monetary figures are in US dollars.)

The data reveals the following:

- The project was expected to complete $4,000,000 worth of work by now.
- The budget spent so far is $3,800,000.
- The value of the work actually completed is $3,200,000.

What is the cost variance (CV)?
questions.explanation:
The CV is –$600,000, which means the project has spent $600,000 more than the value of the work completed. This indicates that the project is over budget.

Cost variance (CV) measures budget performance by comparing the value of completed work to the actual cost.

The formula for CV is:

CV = EV–AC

Earned value (EV) is the value of the work actually completed.

- EV = $3,200,000

Actual cost (AC) is the budget spent so far.

- AC = $3,800,000

$3,200,000 – $3,800,000 = –$600,000

Other options are incorrect.

Based on the formula CV = EV–AC, all other answer choices are incorrect because they do not match the actual calculation.

questions.stem:
A project manager is forming a new project team and learns that key team members and external reviewers are already committed to other projects. Because these resources are controlled by various managers and stakeholders, the project manager needs a structured approach to gain their support and commitment for the new project.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Schedule a meeting to discuss potential conflicts with upper management and request a resolution plan.
Develop a detailed stakeholder engagement plan that outlines how relevant stakeholders will be engaged.
Inform stakeholders about the overtime policy, and warn project managers to expect temporary resource constraints.
Recognize the potential competition for resources and identify tasks that could be deferred for later development.

questions.solutionLine: B. Develop a stakeholder engagement plan that outlines the way relevant stakeholders will be engaged.
questions.explanation:
When resources are controlled by different managers and stakeholders, the project manager should use a structured stakeholder engagement approach to build support, address concerns, and secure commitment. A detailed stakeholder engagement plan should outline the level of engagement required from each stakeholder and specify the nature of their engagement. Having an agreed-upon plan reduces uncertainty from potential resource constraints by aligning project needs with stakeholder expectations.

The other options are incorrect because they are more reactive or partial.

Escalating to upper management may come later, but not as the first structured step. Management cannot make informed decisions in the absence of clear requirements, which should be described in the plan.

Overtime warnings do not solve commitment issues. Attempting to minimize the impact by warning team members to expect overtime does not manage or mitigate the resource constraints. Just informing stakeholders or issuing warnings without a mitigation strategy is likely to be ineffective and can potentially increase tensions between projects.

Deferring tasks is a schedule adjustment, not a method for gaining stakeholder support. Any reductions in response to limited resource availability should be made through formal adjustments to the stakeholder engagement plan.
questions.notes: Solution line wording differs slightly from option B text (verbatim as shown).

questions.stem: A team planned to complete 50 story points in an iteration but only reached 30. What is the schedule performance index (SPI)?
questions.explanation:
To calculate SPI, we use the following formula:

SPI = Earned Value (EV) / Planned Value (PV)

In this case:

EV: 30 story points (actual completed work)

PV: 50 story points (planned work)

In summary, the SPI of 0.6 indicates that the team is performing at 60% of the planned efficiency, meaning they are behind schedule.

The other answer choices are incorrect due to miscalculations.

questions.stem:
A global project pays suppliers in three currencies. Exchange rate volatility was identified as a known risk, and contingency reserves were set aside for it. A temporary shift increases projected costs by 10%, but the impact remains within the approved contingency reserve. Hedging is not permitted.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Implement financial risk response strategies such as hedging in coordination with finance experts.
Work with suppliers to notify them that supplier payments will be delayed until exchange rates stabilize.
Explain to suppliers that their invoices will be paid in U.S. dollars until exchange rates return to normal.
Use the approved contingency reserve to address the cost impact from the identified exchange rate risk.

questions.solutionLine: D. Use the approved contingency reserve to address the cost impact from the identified exchange rate risk.
questions.explanation:
The scenario describes a known risk that was already identified during planning. Exchange rate volatility was recognized in advance, and contingency reserves were specifically set aside for that purpose. Contingency reserves are intended to address the impact of identified risks when they occur. Since the temporary cost increase remains within the approved contingency reserve, the project manager should implement the planned financial response by using that reserve. This is the most appropriate and disciplined action because it follows the risk management plan, stays within authorized limits, and does not require unauthorized changes to procurement terms or supplier relationships.

The other options are incorrect.

The question explicitly states that hedging is not permitted. Even though hedging can be a legitimate response to exchange rate risk in some organizations, it is not available in this case.

Delaying payments is not an appropriate response to the risk described. The project already has an approved reserve to absorb the impact, so there is no reason to disrupt payment obligations, and delaying payment could create new risks, including contract disputes, supplier dissatisfaction, claims, schedule delays, and reputational harm.

If supplier contracts specify payment in particular currencies, the project manager cannot simply decide to pay in another currency for the project’s convenience. That kind of action would likely violate contractual agreements and create legal, commercial, and relationship issues. It also attempts to shift the exchange-rate risk from the buyer to the supplier without negotiation or approval, which is not proper contract management.

questions.stem:
A project manager is overseeing the construction of a new data center and is responsible for determining the optimal development methodology. The project manager needs to evaluate the project’s circumstances and choose the appropriate development approach.

What should the project manager do to achieve this goal?

options.text: Implement structured processes and oversight mechanisms to minimize uncertainty and ensure the project aligns with organizational policies.
Apply the development approach determined by the project management office to align the project to the organization’s business priorities.
Execute a review of similar projects to identify whether a predictive, hybrid, or adaptive approach has been most effective.
Use a suitability filter to assess the project’s characteristics and determine the best fit among predictive, hybrid, or adaptive approaches.

questions.solutionLine: D. Use a suitability filter to assess the project’s characteristics and determine the best fit among predictive, hybrid, or adaptive approaches.
questions.explanation:
A suitability filter is a useful decision-making tool that helps project teams evaluate their unique circumstances. The suitability filter combines its assessment of the project with other data and decision-making tools to ensure that the appropriate approach is selected for each project.

The other options are less effective.

Aligning with organizational policies is an important component of choosing a development methodology, but a rigid application of structures and processes may not fit the project's context or allow for necessary tailoring.

If an organization has a project management office (PMO), it will work with the project team to align the project to the organization’s business priorities and review and approve the development approach. However, not every organization has a PMO, and the project manager and their team are ultimately most familiar with the context of their specific project.

Reviewing past or concurrent projects with similar contexts can provide valuable information when determining a developmental methodology, but no two projects are exactly the same, and it is important to consider all information unique to the current project to determine the optimal approach.

questions.stem:
An architecture firm wants to increase its productivity. The firm has a major project in progress. The Chief Operating Officer (COO) suggests implementing a new time management software. However, the project sponsor is concerned that although the software might improve productivity, it might not support the project’s primary objective of delivering an exceptional customer experience.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Propose a software option that best supports the organization’s need to increase productivity.
Demonstrate the effectiveness of time management training to reach a similar outcome at a lower cost.
Examine the intended outcome with stakeholders and prioritize solutions that support higher-value outcomes.
Reject the suggestion and schedule a stakeholder meeting to determine whether they have other ideas.

questions.solutionLine: C. Examine the intended outcome with stakeholders and prioritize solutions that support higher-value outcomes.
questions.explanation:
The project manager should work with stakeholders to clarify the project's intended outcomes and determine which actions or deliverables best support the overall strategic goals, including the primary objective of enhancing the customer experience. Focusing on priorities and intended outcomes helps guide actions that fulfill all of the project’s goals, including exceptional customer experience, rather than solely on productivity. Although software solutions may achieve the desired productivity outcome, implementing a productivity-focused adjustment may not align with the project’s purpose. Stakeholders must stay aligned on achieving outputs that drive the intended outcome rather than concentrating on a single aspect.

The other options are less effective.

Software may not be the best solution, as productivity can be impacted by many factors.

Proposing a time management software that best supports productivity can help the team find the most effective product, but it may overlook other viable options and trade-offs. While software may seem like the best choice, all factors, including its impact on user experience, should be carefully considered before making a decision. Increasing productivity is important, but it must be balanced with the goal of providing an exceptional customer experience.

Time management training may not lead to higher productivity and may divert time and focus from other areas. Cost reduction is ineffective if the training fails to achieve the desired increase in productivity or negatively impacts the customer experience.

Involving stakeholders and seeking additional input or ideas is generally helpful, but the project manager should not reject the proposed solution without evaluation and review. This could delay the implementation of a solution or overlook a viable solution.

questions.stem:
A project team is completing a software release project, with another release scheduled for the following year. The project manager needs to ensure the team retains the knowledge gained during this project and makes it available as a reference for the next project. The team has documented procedures and created manuals, but they recognize that these do not capture all the tacit knowledge developed during the project. The project manager needs to ensure that as much of the team’s collective knowledge as possible is transferred.

What action should the project manager adopt in this scenario?

options.text: Ensure the manuals and documented procedures are stored in an accessible database for use on the next project.
Conduct brainstorming sessions and retrospectives to identify information that should be collected during the project.
Use project management software to help ensure real-time tracking of milestones across the project's phases.
Define a final delivery point for transferring the software release and its documentation over to the implementation team.

questions.solutionLine: B. Conduct brainstorming sessions and retrospectives to identify information that should be collected during the project.
questions.explanation:
Creating recurring opportunities for knowledge transfer through conversations, brainstorming, and retrospectives or lessons-learned sessions helps identify tacit knowledge gained from the team’s collective experience and make it more explicit.

The other options are less effective.

Although the manuals and documented procedures should be accessible for use on the next project, they do not capture all the collective background knowledge the team has gained from working on this project.

Using management software to track milestones across project phases helps maintain a history, but it does not ensure that other historical information is captured.

Defining a delivery point for transferring the project over to the implementation team is a necessary step in concluding the project, but it does not control how much knowledge is conveyed.

questions.stem:
A project team is preparing a RACI (responsible, accountable, consulted, informed) matrix for stakeholders on an upcoming project. The project manager reviews the chart and tells the team to add the customer as a stakeholder.

Click on the “Stakeholder” below that aligns with the role of the customer on the RACI matrix.

RACI Matrix — Stakeholder(s): One | Two | Three
Create charter: A | I | C
Collect requirements: I | C | R
Submit change request: A | R | C
Develop test plan: C | R | I
R = Responsible  A = Accountable  C = Consulted  I = Informed

options.text: One
Two
Three

questions.solutionLine: Three
questions.explanation:
The stakeholders would be represented on a RACI matrix as follows, based on their typical responsibilities and involvement in the listed activities. Here's how they align with the roles of Responsible (R), Accountable (A), Consulted (C), and Informed (I) for each activity:

Create Charter
Customer: Consulted (C) – Customers are consulted during charter creation to ensure their needs, requirements, and expectations are captured correctly.
SMEs: Informed (I) – SMEs are informed about the charter to understand the scope and expectations, but they are not typically active contributors at this stage.
Sponsor: Accountable (A) – The sponsor is ultimately accountable for approving and endorsing the project charter.

Collect Requirements
Customer: Responsible (R) – Customers actively provide the requirements needed to shape the scope and deliverables of the project.
SMEs: Consulted (C) – SMEs provide specialized knowledge to refine and validate requirements provided by the customer.
Sponsor: Informed (I) – The project sponsor is kept informed about the progress and key insights during requirements collection.

Submit Change Request
Customer: Consulted (C) – Customers are consulted for approvals or suggestions related to changes impacting business needs or project outcomes.
SMEs: Responsible (R) – SMEs are responsible for drafting and preparing the change request based on their domain expertise before submission
Sponsor: Accountable (A) – The sponsor is accountable for approving or rejecting submitted change requests as they relate to project scope, budget, and objectives.

Develop Test Plan
Customer: Informed (I) – Customers are informed about the test plan to understand how their requirements are being validated, but they do not create or contribute directly.
SMEs: Responsible (R) – SMEs are responsible for developing the test plan, as they possess the required knowledge to design the test cases, criteria, and execution strategy.
Sponsor: Consulted (C) – The project sponsor is consulted to provide oversight or ensure the alignment of the test plan with strategic goals.

This structure ensures clear accountability, minimizes role confusion, and promotes stakeholder engagement at the appropriate level for each activity. It also aligns the distribution of responsibility with the strengths and authority of each stakeholder group.

RACI matrix with column Three highlighted as the customer

questions.stem:
A local government office is undertaking a new municipal construction project. With numerous stakeholders involved, clear communication of the project’s objectives is vital. To begin, the project manager needs to clearly outline and communicate how the project’s objectives will be executed, managed, and controlled.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Organize a plan sourcing strategy to determine the scope of work for executing external scoping decisions.
Execute a scope management plan to document how the project scope will be defined, validated, and controlled.
Develop a project schedule to present linked project activities with their planned dates, duration, and resources.
Implement a project management plan to integrate and consolidate all subsidiary plan components.

questions.solutionLine: D. Implement a project management plan to integrate and consolidate all subsidiary plan components.
questions.explanation:
A project management plan is an overarching document that integrates and consolidates all subsidiary components, such as the scope management plan, schedule management plan, cost management plan, and others. By implementing the project management plan, the project manager ensures a centralized source of information that communicates how the project’s objectives will be executed, managed, and controlled. This comprehensive approach aligns multiple aspects of the project and stakeholders, addressing the need for clarity and coordination as outlined in the question.

The other options are incorrect.

A sourcing strategy focuses on decisions related to procurement and external resources. While it is necessary, it is not sufficient on its own to clearly outline and communicate how the project’s objectives will be executed, managed, and controlled.

A scope management plan provides guidelines for scope, but it does not address the need for comprehensive integration and clarity across multiple project areas. Creating and executing this plan is one subsidiary component of the larger project management plan.

Developing a project schedule is essential for project management, but it focuses on scheduling specifics rather than on integrating and communicating overall project objectives across stakeholders.

questions.stem:
A multinational enterprise is bringing a new product to market. As the project nears completion, the project manager is notified of a disagreement among end users regarding the functionality of a specific product feature. The project manager must obtain stakeholder approval in order to close the project.

Which should the project manager do? (Choose 2)

options.text: Request approval to close the project and resolve the issue in the next product iteration.
Meet with the team lead to determine if any issues regarding product features were discovered during testing.
Meet with project stakeholders to review the project's agreed-upon acceptance criteria.
Review the definition of done (DoD) that was agreed upon and documented at the beginning of the project.
Review the project scope to understand the acceptance criteria established at the beginning of the project.

questions.solutionLine: C, D
questions.explanation:
C. Meet with project stakeholders to review the project's agreed-upon acceptance criteria.

D. Review the definition of done (DoD) that was agreed upon and documented at the beginning of the project.

The project manager needs to understand the acceptance criteria and the DoD for the project, and share this information with stakeholders to obtain approval and close the project. The acceptance criteria would outline the set of conditions that are met before deliverables are accepted and can be used to confirm the completeness of the deliverable. The DoD is a checklist of all the criteria that must be met for a deliverable to be considered ready for customer use. This will help determine whether the project meets DoD requirements and whether anything is missing or incomplete.

The other options are less effective.

The project manager should not close the project. They should wait until the next product iteration to work out any issues. If customer satisfaction is not high enough, the product might not go live until further rework.

Meeting with the team lead to discuss product features discovered during testing is helpful, but it does not help obtain stakeholder approval in order to close the project.

The time before project closure is not the time to review the project scope to understand the acceptance criteria. That should have been done at the start of the project and during each project phase. The goal is to verify that the output meets the criteria and is fit for closure, not just to understand the criteria.

questions.stem:
A project team has been developing a new social media platform. The current project phase is nearing completion, and the team is working to finish its tasks and transition to the next phase. The project manager must determine whether the deliverables have been completed successfully.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Compare the finished product with the project’s definition of done (DoD) to ensure it meets all the completion criteria.
Evaluate whether each project component has achieved its intended value as outlined in the value breakdown structure (VBS).
Schedule a meeting with the relevant stakeholders to evaluate the project and determine whether it meets their expectations.
Examine the project backlog to confirm that all prioritized tasks are complete and that no outstanding work remains.

questions.solutionLine: A. Compare the finished product with the project’s definition of done (DoD) to ensure it meets all the completion criteria.
questions.explanation:
A DoD is a shared understanding of the specific criteria that should be met before a piece of work (a user story, feature, or increment) is considered complete and ready for release to the next stage or the customer. Comparing against the DoD ensures it satisfies all predefined completion criteria and meets the agreed-upon standards for quality, functionality, and deliverables. This comparison ensures the project can advance to subsequent stages or be officially closed without leaving any incomplete work.

The other options are incorrect because they each address only a component of the completion requirements.

Although assessing the project’s value, obtaining stakeholder sign-off, and analyzing the project backlog are all important steps in completing a project, none of them alone is sufficient to determine the project’s completion status. The project manager must complete all of these steps and any other items outlined in the DoD to verify that the project’s phase has been successfully completed.

questions.stem:
A project team is implementing a large-scale enterprise resource planning (ERP) system in the manufacturing industry. This is a high-priority project for the organization, in which the executive leadership is involved as project sponsors. The project manager is tasked with aligning expectations among all the relevant stakeholders.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Compare the priorities of executive leadership with those of other stakeholders and identify the common expectations.
Analyze the differing needs and expectations of all stakeholders and prioritize them according to the organizational hierarchy.
Use predictive analytics and data visualization to present documentation to stakeholders and guide them toward the project team’s vision.
Schedule steering committee meetings with the project sponsor and other stakeholders to discuss the project’s objectives.

questions.solutionLine: D. Schedule regular steering committee meetings with the project sponsor and other stakeholders to discuss the project’s objectives.
questions.explanation:
Involving the project sponsor in all important discussions and decisions allows them to exercise decision-making authority while also facilitating collaboration with a representative selection of other relevant stakeholders. This ensures that stakeholder expectations align with both the organization’s broader strategy and the project objectives.

The other options are incorrect.

On a high-profile project, the project sponsor holds the ultimate decision-making authority, but it is still helpful to facilitate discussions with other stakeholders whose priorities and insight may differ. Finding common ground is important, but it is equally important to discuss the areas where expectations differ and reach an agreement.

Although it may be necessary at times to make decisions based on the hierarchy of those involved, it does not facilitate alignment of stakeholder expectations and may negatively impact collaborative communication throughout the project if some stakeholders feel their needs are not valued.

Predictive analytics and data visualization can be powerful tools for gathering documentation to present to stakeholders and for facilitating rapid decision-making, but it is still important to consider shareholders' needs and expectations and to adjust the project objectives as necessary to align with them.

questions.stem:
A project team is developing a critical organizational training initiative. The project manager has consolidated all requirements into the formally approved and baselined project management plan. During execution, unforeseen factors arise that were not captured in the plan. These factors could potentially affect implementation.

What should the project manager do first?

options.text: Conduct a risk analysis on the new factors and submit a formal change request for review and approval by the change control board (CCB).
Apply rolling wave planning techniques to refine detailed deliverables and progressively update the approved project management plan.
Deliver the training initiative as originally planned and document the unforeseen factors that materialized as lessons learned for future projects.
Increase contingency and management reserves to account for unforeseen uncertainties and reduce the need for mid-project plan revisions.

questions.solutionLine: A. Conduct a risk analysis on the new factors and submit a formal change request for review and approval by the change control board (CCB).
questions.explanation:
The first step is to conduct a risk analysis to quantify their potential effects and assess their severity. This analysis forms the foundation for preparing a formal change request. By submitting the change request for review and approval by the CCB, the project manager complies with the formal change control process required for a baselined plan.

The other options are incorrect.

Rolling wave planning doesn’t apply here. Rolling wave planning is used in iterative, adaptive methods, where near-term work is planned in more detail while longer-term work is progressively elaborated. However, in this scenario, the project management plan is already baselined and formally approved. These unforeseen factors represent changes, not planned refinements, and thus require formal handling first.

Delivering the training initiative as planned is not proactive and does not address the impact of unforeseen factors in real time, which could jeopardize the project's success. Documenting lessons learned is important, but it is done after the project is completed, not as a solution for mid-project issues.

Reserves are typically planned during project initiation and are not arbitrarily increased during project execution. Any increase to reserves must also follow formal change control processes.

questions.stem:
During a sprint review, the project manager presents a burndown chart. The line depicting the actual amount accomplished remains far below the expected trend for most of the sprint. The sponsor demands action, but the scrum master insists the team should self-organize. The product sponsor worries stakeholders will lose confidence if this pattern continues.

What should the project manager do? (Refer to the chart)

options.text: Recruit temporary team members to accelerate delivery and reduce the sprint backlog in order to satisfy stakeholders.
Escalate the concern to senior management and request approval to adjust the scope and modify the sprint commitment.
Support the scrum master and allow the team to self-organize, using the retrospective for improvements and learning.
Extend the sprint duration to allow the team to complete all committed work and demonstrate progress to stakeholders.

questions.solutionLine: C. Support the scrum master and allow the team to self-organize, using the retrospective for improvements and learning.
questions.explanation:
The project manager should let the team self-organize, inspect in the retrospective, and adapt future planning. This prioritizes adhering to agile principles by allowing the team to use retrospectives to inspect and adapt. It promotes accountability, continuous improvement, and collaborative problem-solving.

The other options are incorrect.

Adding new members mid-sprint disrupts team stability and violates agile principles.

Escalation is unnecessary. Backlog and sprint scope are managed by the team and product owner, not senior management.

The sprint length is fixed. Extending sprints to accommodate unfinished work reduces predictability and sets a negative precedent for future sprints.

questions.stem:
A project manager at a mining company has been assigned the first engineering project since the company implemented a comprehensive new environmental policy. While integrating the required sustainability measures into the project management plan, the project manager becomes concerned that internal and external stakeholders may view these mandatory requirements as constraints that will slow progress.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Offset the cost of sustainability practices with the projected cost of failing regulatory compliance.
Provide tools that will enable the team to measure and manage the sustainability of their work.
Educate the stakeholders about sustainability to ensure all parties are aligned with the environmental goals.
Create opportunities for innovation by encouraging the team to develop resource-efficient solutions.

questions.solutionLine: A. Offset the cost of sustainability practices with the projected cost of failing regulatory compliance.
questions.explanation:
Offsetting the cost of sustainability practices against the projected cost of failing regulatory compliance is a practical approach grounded in financial reasoning. It focuses on demonstrating the business case for sustainability by comparing the expenses of implementing sustainability practices to the potentially higher costs of non-compliance with regulations.

The other options are incorrect.

While providing tools to measure and manage sustainability is operationally sound and important for execution, it addresses the team’s needs rather than stakeholder concerns.

Educating stakeholders about sustainability emphasizes education and awareness, which are important, but it does not directly address concerns about perceived limitations, as measured by common, relatable metrics such as cost.

Encouraging creativity within the team is valuable for project execution, but it is primarily internally focused. It doesn’t directly address the core issue of how stakeholders perceive sustainability as a constraint.

questions.stem:
A project manager is preparing for a complex new project with significant uncertainty. The team is gathering requirements, analyzing stakeholder needs, and attempting to define multi-layered dependencies.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Allow time in the schedule for delays because incorporating differing opinions might slow progress.
Elicit advice from individuals outside the project team to help the team maintain its momentum.
Seek guidance from subject matter experts (SMEs) who can help identify uncertainties and blind spots.
Plan to involve an external quality assurance auditor throughout the project to ensure consistency.

questions.solutionLine: C. Seek guidance from subject matter experts (SMEs) who can help identify uncertainties and blind spots.
questions.explanation:
In the initial stages, SMEs can highlight potential pitfalls or constraints, aiding in risk identification and robust planning. SMEs can help identify uncertainties and blind spots that the project team might miss, increasing the project’s efficiency. SMEs can provide reliable context, real-world impacts, and expose hidden dependencies that may be overlooked by the team. This is especially valuable in complex and uncertain environments.

The other options are incorrect.

Arbitrarily adding time without working to better understand the project's full scope, dependencies, and uncertainties is not a proactive approach. Gaining insights can increase efficiency and shorten the project’s timeline.

It might be appropriate to involve external auditors or experts, depending on the specific expertise required for the project. However, seeking only outside advice is shortsighted, overlooks team member expertise, and eliminates team involvement.

Engaging an auditor for the project's duration may be unnecessary, ineffective at addressing these initial planning needs, and costly.

questions.stem:
A government contractor is awarded a project that involves multiple requirements in various compliance categories. The project sponsor asks the project manager to ensure compliance by allocating resources effectively. The project management office cautions that noncompliance could result in significant penalties.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Categorize the compliance requirements based on the penalties that apply if standards are not met.
Prioritize compliance efforts according to their significance and potential impact on the project.
Organize a workshop with stakeholders to gather insights from their past experience with compliance regulations.
Allocate the majority of resources to the compliance categories that pose the greatest risk if standards are not met.

questions.solutionLine: B. Prioritize compliance efforts according to their significance and potential impact on the project.
questions.explanation:
Prioritizing compliance efforts according to their significance and potential impact directly ties resource allocation to the requirements’ significance and impact. By identifying high-priority requirements with substantial impact, the project manager can focus efforts where they matter most. This approach ensures a structured and strategic distribution of resources based on both risk and relevance.

The other options are incorrect.

While categorizing requirements can provide clarity, it is only a preparatory step. It doesn’t ensure effective resource allocation, address the broader challenge of prioritization, or directly help mitigate penalties.

Workshops and stakeholder engagement can add value, but this option mainly collects information and is more general rather than focusing specifically on compliance prioritization or resource allocation.

Prioritizing compliance efforts based on their importance and potential impact might lead to neglecting other key compliance areas, which could cause problems in fulfilling less critical but still mandatory requirements.
questions.notes: Last explanation paragraph appears to describe option D but is shown verbatim as in source.

questions.stem:
A project manager is leading a small internal project with limited scope, low complexity, and minimal risks. Despite this, the sponsor insists on a comprehensive, detailed risk management plan. The project manager worries that creating such a plan will consume limited resources, delay deliverables, and reduce efficiency.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Develop a comprehensive risk management plan to demonstrate rigorous and thorough governance practices.
Confirm that all risks are documented in a comprehensive, detailed risk register, regardless of the project’s size.
Reallocate resources and request additional budget approval to prepare the comprehensive risk plan required.
Explain that the project scope does not justify a detailed plan and suggest adopting an adaptive approach instead.

questions.solutionLine: D. Explain that the project scope does not justify a detailed plan and suggest adopting an adaptive approach instead.
questions.explanation:
An adaptive approach should be considered due to limited scope, timeline, and resource constraints. This aligns with the principles of tailoring project management practices to the specific needs of the project. While risk management is critical, the level of rigor applied should be proportional to the project’s scope, complexity, and risks. Instead of investing extensive resources into creating a comprehensive risk management plan, the project manager should propose fit-for-purpose risk management practices that improve efficiency without compromising governance. An adaptive approach allows the project manager to manage risks appropriately while maintaining efficiency and focusing resources where they are needed most.

The other options are incorrect.

Developing a comprehensive risk management plan shows governance, but it wastes resources and time, leading to inefficiency and delays, especially when the risks are minimal and the project is simple.

A risk register is valuable, but creating a detailed one for a project with minimal risks is not proportional to the project's size or risk.

Requesting additional budget for a minor internal project is unlikely to be a practical or justified approach.

questions.stem:
A technology company is designing a new product. The project team wants to incorporate renewable resources to meet sustainability goals and ensure compliance with evolving regulatory shifts. Some of the stakeholders are reluctant and worry that incorporating renewable resources will increase the cost of the project. The project manager must align the stakeholders' vision with the team’s sustainability goals.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Ask the project sponsor to communicate the organization’s sustainability expectations to the relevant stakeholders.
Demonstrate the value of sustainable technology by emphasizing decreased financial risks, improved social reputation, and long-term savings.
Organize a mandatory company meeting to encourage discussions about the impact of sustainability goals.
Compare the business case, project charter, and other formal project documents to identify the key performance indicators.

questions.solutionLine: B. Demonstrate the value of sustainable technology by emphasizing decreased financial risks, improved social reputation, and long-term savings.
questions.explanation:
Sustainability education and collaboration facilitate stakeholder engagement by fostering accountability, aligning scope with organizational goals and societal needs, and enhancing stakeholder trust. This approach will benefit the team during the execution of the project and deliver lasting value to the organization, improving its reputation and resilience after the project life cycle is complete.

The other options are incorrect.

Asking the project sponsor to communicate the organization's sustainability expectations does not foster a collaborative approach with stakeholders. Although it may be necessary to engage the project sponsor to communicate the organization’s expectations, doing so does not inherently address the stakeholders’ concerns about cost or align their vision with the project team.

Engaging the broader community may be a key part of identifying social and environmental sustainability needs, but it will not inherently address cost concerns. Adding more stakeholders will also broaden the scope of project management and may increase the cost and complexity of managing the project.

Identifying key performance indicators will allow the team to compare how the project is lining up against its stated goals and intended value as the project progresses, but it does not inherently present the cost-value benefits of sustainability or facilitate communication and trust-building with stakeholders.

questions.stem:
A nongovernmental organization operating internationally is launching a medium-sized global project. The project team is made up of stakeholders from diverse cultural backgrounds and regions. To guarantee consistent stakeholder engagement and collaboration, the project manager must implement inclusive communication strategies.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Hold daily coordination meetings to promote real-time collaboration and stakeholder engagement.
Foster open communication by implementing informal channels to facilitate rapid decision-making.
Leverage large language models (LLMs) and generative AI (Gen AI) to automate stakeholder communication.
Schedule multilingual updates and monthly virtual forums to foster stakeholder engagement and collect feedback.

questions.solutionLine: D. Schedule multilingual updates and monthly virtual forums to foster stakeholder engagement and collect feedback.
questions.explanation:
Multilingual updates ensure that stakeholders from different regions and cultural backgrounds all have access to relevant information and formal updates. Monthly virtual forums provide opportunities for stakeholders to meet virtually with the project team and communicate directly without creating an unreasonable scheduling burden due to differing time zones.

The other options are less effective.

Daily coordination meetings are difficult to plan and implement on a global scale when stakeholders may be located in different time zones. Asynchronous collaboration is necessary when conducting a project on a global scale.

Informal communication channels can be a useful tool for soliciting immediate answers to questions, but may cause conflict when engaging stakeholders from different cultural backgrounds. Many cultures prioritize a more hierarchical approach to organizational structure, so formal communications may be preferred.

LLMs and AI can be used to provide translations and produce artifacts for communication with stakeholders, but the risk of incorporating these technologies must be assessed through an organizational decision-making process. Relying solely on AI can also lead to misrepresentation of information, confusion, and misalignment. This approach is focused on one-way communication, but AI would not be the best strategy for collecting feedback.

questions.stem:
A major retailer known for its environmentally conscious branding is launching a new collaboration that will attract significant public attention. It is important to the organization’s image and brand recognition that the collaboration aligns with its broader goals. The project manager needs to ensure the project aligns with the organization’s vision and expectations throughout the project timeline.

What should the project manager do?

options.text: Organize weekly newsletter reports to stakeholders, communicating progress and soliciting feedback on the project’s developing vision.
Schedule regular check-ins with the project sponsor to align with business objectives, report progress, and facilitate executive decision-making.
Compare progress and deliverables against the vision statement and other documentation developed during the project’s initiation phase.
Implement a project charter and facilitate daily meetings with the team to update it as the vision evolves throughout project development.

questions.solutionLine: B. Schedule regular check-ins with the project sponsor to align with business objectives, report progress, and facilitate executive decision-making.
questions.explanation:
The project sponsor’s responsibilities include communicating the organization’s ongoing vision, goals, or expectations to the project manager and project team, and are critical for achieving environmental, social, and governance goals. Regularly checking in with the project sponsor ensures that all decisions made regarding the project align with the greater goals of the organization and that any changes in vision are efficiently communicated to the project team so they can adjust their work accordingly.

The other options are incorrect.

Although communicating with stakeholders about the project’s ongoing progress and vision is an important component of project management, doing so does not guarantee that the project’s vision stays current and aligned with the business objectives of the greater organization. Soliciting stakeholder feedback is crucial to ensuring the project runs smoothly, but it does not keep the project’s vision aligned on its own.

A vision statement and other documentation developed during the project initiation phase are useful tools for comparing progress against the initially stated goals, but those documents must be updated in accordance with any feedback from the project sponsor to ensure that both the documentation and the project remain up to date.

The project sponsor is responsible for ensuring the project is aligned with any changes in organizational goals. Daily briefings with the project team are useful for ensuring development is proceeding smoothly, and all changes are documented, but any changes to the overall vision must be made with the input of the project sponsor. Otherwise, the project runs the risk of failing to meet the greater organizational goals.
